_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for SO retrospectives (retro/build_so.py). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date: a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR records no time before 2003). Southern Company's earnings 8-Ks of Q2 2007 to Q3 2017 were accepted before the open or during the session on the release day (a Wednesday or Thursday, and Mondays 2012-11-05 and 2016-10-31), and the 10-Ks weeks after the Q4 releases, so a Q4 print carries its year's actuals (fy_actual) until the 10-K. No filing guides EPS, revenue or a margin in numbers (to 2011 the releases say earnings guidance is discussed on the analyst call; from Q2 2016 they point to earnings slides with an estimate or guidance on the company's website; no transcript or slides are filed). The company's EPS excluding only one-offs, where a filing states it, is in 'eps_bases' and the prints' notes (retro/README.md, 'SO 2010-2013' and 'SO 2014-2017'). Generated by a script from row strings of the filings (each checked with retro/tools/verbatim.py); every growth rate, margin, margin change and rule-T value is computed. See retro/README.md, 'SO'.

distributions.note: the spin-off of Mirant: 'On April 2, 2001, the tax-free distribution of Mirant shares was completed at a ratio of approximately 0.4 for every share of SOUTHERN common stock held at record date.' (SO4); Yahoo books it as a 10000:6109 split on 2001-04-03, the first day the stock traded without it; it is not a split, so its factor is undone for the days before and prices stay as traded (the MAR, PFE and BMY 'distributions' rule).
